name: Utility-scale solar power cost
summary: Utility-scale solar is the large farms that feed the grid. The usual yardstick is levelized cost of energy: a lifetime average price per megawatt-hour that folds in building and running the plant. In many markets that cost has fallen by roughly half every several years since the mid-2010s. The chart is US dollars per megawatt-hour — lower means cheaper bulk solar.
trendSummary: Utility solar electricity costs fell into the lowest-cost bulk power tier in sunny markets.
